rules.title: San Francisco Just Cause Eviction Requirements
rules.requirement: A landlord in San Francisco may only evict a tenant from a covered rental unit if one of 17 specific 'just cause' reasons applies, such as nonpayment of rent, owner move-in, demolition, or Ellis Act withdrawal.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to rental units covered by the Rent Ordinance, including some units otherwise exempt from rent increase limitations (e.g., newer construction, Costa-Hawkins-eligible units, and units regulated by another agency).
rules.quoted_span: In order to evict a tenant from a rental unit covered by the Rent Ordinance, a landlord must have a "just cause" reason that is the dominant motive for pursuing the eviction.

rules.title: San Francisco Rent Increase Limitation Exemptions (new construction, Costa-Hawkins, other agency regulation)
rules.requirement: Units that first obtained a Certificate of Occupancy after June 13, 1979, units eligible for a rent increase under the state Costa-Hawkins Rental Housing Act, and some units where rent is regulated by another government agency are exempt from San Francisco's rent increase limitations, even though they remain subject to just cause eviction protections.
rules.coverage_conditions: Rent increase limits generally apply to residential rental units covered by the Rent Ordinance, excluding newer construction, Costa-Hawkins-eligible units, and some units regulated by another agency.
rules.exemptions: Newly constructed units with Certificate of Occupancy after June 13, 1979; units eligible for rent increase under Costa-Hawkins Rental Housing Act; some units where rent is regulated by another government agency.
rules.quoted_span: This includes tenancies in newly constructed rental units that first obtained a Certificate of Occupancy after June 13, 1979, tenancies that are eligible for a rent increase under the Costa-Hawkins Rental Housing Act, and some tenancies where the rent is regulated by another government agency.

coverage.other_unknown_factor: whether the unit is eligible for a rent increase under the state Costa-Hawkins Rental Housing Act or has its rent regulated by another government agency

rules.conflict_note: The specific Ordinance section number for the rent increase limitation itself is not stated in this chunk; citation uses the general chapter reference.
